old_caption: The video opens with a completely dark scene, setting a mysterious and suspenseful tone. A small flame is visible on the left side of the frame, flickering gently against the black background. Another small flame is visible in the distance, to the right of the first one. The flame on the left remains largely unchanged in shape and size throughout the sequence. The two flames cast a warm, orange glow that contrasts sharply with the surrounding darkness. The scene is static, with no camera motion, focusing solely on these two flames as they illuminate the otherwise pitch-black environment. The overall atmosphere is one of quiet intensity, with the flickering flames serving as the sole source of light and movement in the scene.
original_wisa_caption: The video opens with a completely dark scene, setting a mysterious and suspenseful tone. Gradually, a small flame appears on the left side of the frame, flickering gently against the black background. This flame grows slightly larger and more defined, casting a warm, orange glow that contrasts sharply with the surrounding darkness. As the video progresses, another small flame emerges in the distance, to the right of the first one. This second flame also begins to grow, becoming more prominent and steady. The two flames continue to burn, each growing larger and more defined, while the rest of the scene remains shrouded in darkness. The camera remains stationary throughout, focusing solely on these two flames as they illuminate the otherwise pitch-black environment. The overall atmosphere is one of quiet intensity, with the flickering flames serving as the sole source of light and movement in the scene.
caption: A tall, narrow orange-yellow flame burns against a black frame, its base anchored low on the left, the tip rising and flickering. The flame is already alight when the clip opens and still burns as it ends, showing no ignition or extinction. Over the excerpt the tip, starting left-leaning, gradually shifts rightward relative to the fixed base, so the flame sways from a left-leaning posture toward an upright, slightly right-leaning one. Its height stretches a little early on and then holds roughly steady, while the body's brightness and width pulse subtly frame to frame. To the right, a smaller dimmer orange ember appears and fades, flickering in and out rather than translating. Three faint points of light—a white dot near the upper center, a white dot at the far right, and a tiny orange speck mid-frame—stay pinned at identical positions throughout. The stationary background confirms the camera does not move. The flame's own sway and flicker remain the only visible motion.

without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
